Definition: from G1223 and a derivative of G5495; to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay violent hands upon:--kill, slay.
BiblicalUsage: To lay violent hands on a man is what the rulers did to the apostles and what the Jews tried to do to Paul. Peter charges them with slaying Jesus by wicked hands, and Paul's enemies in the temple seized him and sought to kill him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that violent hands tell the truth about a heart; the men who laid hands on the apostles and on Paul were not defending the truth; they were defending their own power, and God turned their violence into a witness.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
